survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS Starting Strong 2024 note reports descriptive survey results from questionnaires administered to ECEC staff and setting leaders in New Zealand, rather than estimating student achievement models. The note states that due to low response rates in New Zealand, the results represent respondents included in the sample and are not representative of the full population of ECEC staff and leaders. The document does not report the specific complex survey design variables or weight identifiers (e.g., sampling weights or replicate weights), so the exact weighting approach cannot be verified from the provided text. For analysts using the underlying TALIS Starting Strong 2024 database, the appropriate approach would be to apply the survey weights supplied with the database for each ECEC level (pre-primary ISCED 02 and under-3 settings) and to follow the report’s annex guidance on indicator construction and sampling coverage.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this note does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes with PV-based scaling; it reports questionnaire-based indicators (e.g., training topics, time use, job satisfaction, stress sources) and leader/staff self-reports. Missing-data handling is not reported in the provided excerpt because the note functions as a participant country results summary rather than a methodological paper detailing imputation or deletion rules for item nonresponse. sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note reports results for New Zealand only for respondents included in the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 sample; it explicitly cautions that low response rates mean the results are not representative of the full population of ECEC staff and leaders. The TALIS Starting Strong 2024 data in New Zealand cover multiple ECEC setting types by age group: home-based education and care services are included only for the under-age-3 sample; centre-based education and care services and play centres are included for children age 0–6; and kindergartens are included for children age 2–6. The note also states that no data are available from kindergartens and play centres in the under-age-3 sample, while data are available in the pre-primary (ISCED 02) sample for these setting types.

data.outcome_summary: TALIS Starting Strong 2024 is an OECD large-scale survey of early childhood education and care (ECEC) staff and setting leaders, using questionnaires to capture background, training, daily work, and well-being. In this New Zealand results note, indicators are reported separately for pre-primary settings (ISCED level 02) and for settings for children under age 3, with coverage varying by setting type (e.g., kindergartens and play centres are not available in the under-3 sample). The note emphasizes descriptive findings such as high shares of staff reporting job-embedded training and collaborative learning, substantial training coverage on special education needs and home-language differences, and common leader stressors related to administrative work and changing requirements. It also reports workforce-related patterns including high job satisfaction but lower perceived societal value and salary satisfaction, alongside gendered workforce composition and absence rates. A key limitation is that, due to low response rates, the New Zealand results represent respondents in the sample rather than the full population, and the note does not provide model-based performance metrics or PV-based scaling.
